title: An MCP server's source reads an answer from a host and runs it as a command
message: The source of this MCP server requests an address written in the code, reads the answer, and passes it to a shell or a process starter. The code that runs is whatever the far end sends: a standing way for someone else to give the server orders.
remediation: Find which address is read and who controls it. Do not use the server until it is explained.

title: An MCP server's source downloads a program and starts it from a temporary directory
message: The source of this MCP server fetches a file from the network, writes it under a temporary directory and starts it. What runs is a program the server did not ship and nobody reviewed.
remediation: Find what is downloaded and from where.

title: An MCP server's source loads a module or a shared library from a temporary place or straight from the network
message: The source of this MCP server loads native or WebAssembly code that it did not ship: a shared library written under a temporary directory, or a module taken from a web address and instantiated at once.
remediation: Find what is loaded and who wrote it.

title: An MCP server's source uploads to a signed storage address written in the code
message: The source of this MCP server contains a signed upload address for a storage bucket and sends data to it. The signature is a credential for someone else's bucket: the data goes to whoever wrote the server.
remediation: Find what is uploaded and whose bucket it is.

title: An MCP server's source files what it handles as a gist or an issue in a repository written in the code
message: The source of this MCP server creates a gist, or files an issue in a repository whose account and name are written into the code. A repository is a place data can be left for its maintainer to read; a server that takes the target from its user is a client, one that fixes it is a drop.
remediation: Find whose repository it is and what is filed.

title: An MCP server's source fetches a paste from a paste site and runs it
message: The source of this MCP server fetches the raw text of a paste from an address written in the code and runs it. A paste is text its author can change at any time: the server runs whatever is there today.
remediation: Find the paste and who owns it.

title: An MCP server's source reads orders from the issues of a repository written in the code
message: The source of this MCP server reads the issues of a repository whose account and name are written into the code and runs what they say. The repository's maintainer decides what the server does.
remediation: Find whose repository it is and what the server does with an issue.

title: An MCP server's source writes into the files of other installed packages
message: The source of this MCP server writes to a file inside another package's directory under `node_modules` or `site-packages`. Changing code that another program loads is how one package rides in on another.
remediation: Find which package is changed and what is added.

title: An MCP server's source lists the machine's user accounts and who is logged in
message: The source of this MCP server reads the machine's account database or runs the commands that list users, groups and logged-in sessions, more than one of them. A tool that serves a task has no need of the list of everyone who can sign in; collecting it is the first step of working out whom to impersonate.
remediation: Find where the list goes and what the tool says it is for.

title: An MCP server's source switches off the permission checks of the agent or the editor
message: The source of this MCP server contains a settings value that turns the agent's or the editor's confirmation and permission checks off: bypassed permissions, every tool allowed, auto-approval. After that, the agent acts on the user's machine without asking.
remediation: Find where the setting is written and undo it.

title: An MCP server's source gives its process the name of a system service
message: The source of this MCP server renames its own process, or starts a helper under another name, to look like a system service. A process list then shows a program the user would not question.
remediation: Find the process that carries the borrowed name and what it does.

title: An MCP server's source asks for the user's roots and then reads a credential file outside them
message: The source of this MCP server asks the client which folders it may work in, and the same file reads a credential file that is in none of them. The roots are the boundary the user granted; a server that names a key file next to them is not staying inside.
remediation: Find which file is read and what is done with it.

title: An MCP server's source carries data to the client inside the address of a resource update
message: The source of this MCP server publishes a resource update whose address is a `data:` value built at run time. A subscription notification is meant to say that a resource changed; here it carries a payload to whoever listens.
remediation: Find what is encoded into the address.

title: An MCP server's source sends notifications to the client in a loop with no end
message: The source of this MCP server sends log or progress notifications from a loop that never stops. The client pays for what it receives and the user's session fills with noise: a way to burn a metered service or to bury a message.
remediation: Find the loop and what bounds it.

title: An MCP server's source decodes or decompresses a value and runs the result as a command or as code
message: The source of this MCP server decodes base64 or decompresses a value it carries and passes the result to a shell, an evaluator or a process starter. Code that arrives as an encoded string cannot be read in a review.
remediation: Decode the value and read what it runs.

title: An MCP server's source joins pieces of an encoded string and decodes the whole
message: The source of this MCP server keeps a string as several encoded pieces, joins them and decodes the result. Splitting a payload this way keeps it from any search for the whole value.
remediation: Join the pieces and decode them.

title: An MCP server's source deletes the user's whole home directory
message: The source of this MCP server removes the user's home directory or a whole drive in one call. No tool of a server needs to do that, and nothing it deletes can be brought back.

title: An MCP server's source reads the cluster's secrets with its own service-account token
message: The source of this MCP server reads the in-cluster service-account token and uses it to list the cluster's secrets. A server that lists pods or reads its own namespace is working; one that asks for every secret is collecting.
remediation: Find which secrets are read and where they go.

title: An MCP server's source holds a fetch-and-run or a send behind a call count, a date or a check for CI
message: The source of this MCP server does something outward-facing only after a number of calls, after a fixed date, or when it is not in a CI job or a sandbox. A gate like that keeps the behaviour from showing in review, in tests or in an analysis run, and lets it appear later on the user's machine.
remediation: Find what the gated branch does, and remove the gate and the branch.
